name: LINE
description: Draws straight segments between picked points, with each segment created as a separate object. The bread-and-butter drafting tool for setting out walls, gridlines and quick construction geometry.

name: PLINE
description: Draws a polyline: a chain of line and arc segments that behaves as a single object. Architects prefer it over LINE for wall outlines, site boundaries and anything that will later be offset, hatched or measured as one entity.

name: POLYGON
description: Creates a regular polygon with 3 to 1024 sides, either inscribed in or circumscribed about a reference circle, or defined by one edge. Handy for column profiles, bolt patterns and paving modules.

name: RECTANG
description: Draws a rectangular closed polyline from two corner points, with options for fillet or chamfer corners, rotation and exact dimensions. A faster route to rooms, panels and title blocks than four separate lines.

name: ARC
description: Creates an arc using combinations of start, centre, end, angle, radius and direction. The default three-point method suits tracing curved walls; the start-centre-end method is the usual pick for door swings.

name: CIRCLE
description: Draws a circle by centre and radius, diameter, two or three points, or tangency to existing objects. Used constantly for columns, trees, service penetrations and setting-out radii.

name: ELLIPSE
description: Creates an ellipse or elliptical arc from axis endpoints, or an isometric circle when isometric drafting is active. Useful for ramps in plan, oval rooflights and 2D isometric details.

name: SPLINE
description: Draws a smooth NURBS curve through fit points or by control vertices. Reach for it when tracing site contours, landscape edges or any freeform profile that lines and arcs cannot follow gracefully.

name: XLINE
description: Creates a construction line of infinite length through a point, optionally horizontal, vertical, angled, bisecting or offset. Drafters use xlines as temporary datums and projection lines between plan, section and elevation.

name: RAY
description: Draws a construction line that starts at a point and extends infinitely in one direction only. A tidier alternative to XLINE when projecting from a fixed origin such as a vanishing point or datum level.

name: POINT
description: Places a point object at a picked or typed coordinate, displayed according to the current point style. Common for survey stations and setting-out markers that can be snapped to with the Node osnap.

name: DIVIDE
description: Places point objects or blocks at an equal number of intervals along a line, arc, polyline or spline. Ideal for spacing balusters, mullions or planting evenly along an edge.

name: MEASURE
description: Places point objects or blocks along an object at a specified repeating distance rather than an equal count. Use it to set out fixings, fence posts or stud centres at a fixed spacing.

name: HATCH
description: Fills an enclosed area or selected boundary with a pattern, solid or user-defined fill. The standard way to show materials in section, floor finishes and poché on plans.

name: GRADIENT
description: Fills a closed area with a one- or two-colour gradient instead of a hatch pattern. Useful for presentation plans, sky tones in elevations and subtle shading without leaving AutoCAD.

name: REGION
description: Converts closed loops of lines, arcs and polylines into 2D region objects that support union, subtract and intersect. Useful for accurate area calculations and as profiles for 3D extrusion.

name: BOUNDARY
description: Creates a closed polyline or region by picking a point inside an enclosed area, tracing the surrounding edges automatically. A quick way to extract room outlines for area schedules without redrawing them.

name: DONUT
description: Draws a filled ring or solid dot defined by inside and outside diameters. Traditionally used for terminal points, drainage symbols and heavy dots on diagrams.

name: REVCLOUD
description: Draws a revision cloud freehand, rectangular or polygonal, or converts an existing closed object into one. The standard graphic for flagging amended areas on issued drawings alongside a revision triangle.

name: WIPEOUT
description: Creates a polygonal mask that blanks out whatever sits beneath it, with an optional visible frame. Drafters use wipeouts behind labels and symbols so text stays legible over dense linework.

name: DRAWORDER
description: Changes which objects display in front of or behind others, including bring-to-front and send-to-back options. Essential for keeping hatches under linework and wipeouts under text.

name: HELIX
description: Creates a 2D spiral or 3D helix defined by base radius, top radius, height and turns. Typically used as a sweep path for spiral stairs, ramps and coiled elements.

name: MLINE
description: Draws multiple parallel lines in one pass using a saved multiline style. A legacy but still handy tool for cavity walls and partitions in pure 2D drafting.

name: TABLE
description: Inserts a table object with rows, columns, formulas and optional data links to spreadsheets. The native way to build door schedules, drawing issue sheets and area tables that stay editable.

name: MTEXT
description: Creates a multiline text object inside a defined boundary, with an in-place editor for formatting, columns, bullets and fields. The default choice for general notes and specification text on drawings.

name: TEXT
description: Places single-line text, with each line created as an independent object and live preview as you type. Quicker than MTEXT for short labels such as room names, levels and grid references.

name: MOVE
description: Relocates selected objects by a base point and second point, or by typed displacement. One of the first commands every drafter learns and among the most used every day.

name: COPY
description: Duplicates selected objects to one or more new positions, repeating until you press Enter, with an Array option for evenly spaced copies. The workhorse for repeating fittings, furniture and details across a plan.

name: ROTATE
description: Spins selected objects about a base point by a typed angle or a reference angle picked from existing geometry. The Reference option is the trick for squaring up survey drawings that arrive slightly askew.

name: SCALE
description: Enlarges or shrinks objects uniformly about a base point by a factor or by reference to a known length. The Reference option is invaluable for rescaling imported PDFs and survey images to a measured dimension.

name: STRETCH
description: Moves the vertices caught inside a crossing window while keeping connected geometry attached, lengthening or shortening objects in one motion. The classic way to widen a room or shift a door opening without redrawing walls.

name: TRIM
description: Cuts objects back to the edges they cross, either against selected cutting edges or, in Quick mode, everything in view. Paired with EXTEND (hold Shift to swap between them) it is the core clean-up tool for junctions and openings.

name: EXTEND
description: Lengthens objects until they meet a boundary edge, the mirror image of TRIM and reachable from it by holding Shift. Used constantly to close gaps where wall lines stop short of a junction.

name: FILLET
description: Joins two objects with an arc of a set radius, or with radius zero simply squares them into a clean corner. The zero-radius fillet is many drafters' fastest way to tidy intersecting wall lines.

name: CHAMFER
description: Connects two lines with an angled bevel defined by distances or a distance and angle. Used for splayed corners, arris details and steelwork bevels; with zero distances it squares corners like FILLET.

name: BLEND
description: Creates a smooth spline bridging the free ends of two open curves, with tangent or curvature continuity. Useful for fairing a transition between a drawn kerb line and an existing survey edge.

name: OFFSET
description: Creates a parallel copy of a line, polyline, arc or circle at a set distance or through a picked point. The fundamental tool for wall thicknesses, cavity lines and stepped setbacks.

name: MIRROR
description: Reflects objects about a two-point axis, keeping or deleting the originals. Perfect for handed flats, symmetrical facades and swapping a door swing; the MIRRTEXT variable controls whether text flips too.

name: ARRAY
description: Creates an associative rectangular, polar or path array of selected objects that can be re-edited later through its grips and contextual ribbon. The umbrella command behind repeating columns, seating and facade modules.

name: ARRAYRECT
description: Distributes copies of objects in rows and columns with editable counts and spacing. The direct route to structural grids, ceiling tiles and car parking layouts.

name: ARRAYPOLAR
description: Copies objects evenly around a centre point through a full circle or set angle. Used for radial column grids, spiral stair treads and circular seating plans.

name: ARRAYPATH
description: Distributes copies of objects along a line, polyline, spline or other path, dividing it evenly or at a set spacing. Ideal for lighting along a corridor, trees along a drive or balusters on a curved stair.

name: EXPLODE
description: Breaks a compound object such as a block, polyline, table or dimension into its constituent parts. Use it sparingly: exploded blocks and dimensions lose the intelligence that makes them easy to manage.

name: JOIN
description: Merges collinear lines, contiguous arcs, polylines and splines into a single object, converting where necessary. The quick fix for fragmented outlines before offsetting, hatching or measuring them.

name: BREAK
description: Removes a portion of an object between two picked points, or splits it at a single point without removing anything. Handy for gapping lines around text or dividing a long wall line for separate treatment.

name: LENGTHEN
description: Changes the length of an open object by a delta, percentage, total length or dynamic drag. Faster than TRIM or EXTEND when there is no convenient boundary edge to work against.

name: ALIGN
description: Moves, rotates and optionally scales objects in one operation by matching pairs of source and destination points. The fastest way to drop a surveyed outbuilding or furniture block onto its correct position and orientation.

name: PEDIT
description: Edits polylines: joining segments, changing width, adding or moving vertices, and fitting curves. Its Join option, with a fuzz distance, is the classic repair for outlines that will not hatch or offset cleanly.

name: ERASE
description: Deletes the selected objects from the drawing, equivalent to selecting them and pressing Delete. Removed objects can be recovered immediately with OOPS even after later commands.

name: OOPS
description: Restores the most recently erased objects without unwinding any commands run since, unlike UNDO. Also brings back source objects removed by the BLOCK or WBLOCK commands.

name: MATCHPROP
description: Copies properties from a source object to others: layer, colour, linetype, and optionally text, dimension and hatch settings. The quickest way to bring rogue objects into line with drawing standards.

name: OVERKILL
description: Deletes duplicate or overlapping lines, arcs and polylines and merges partially overlapping collinear segments. Run it on drawings received from others to slim files and stop double lines confusing snaps and hatches.

name: REVERSE
description: Flips the direction of a line, polyline or spline without changing its geometry. Matters when direction drives something else, such as linetype text orientation or an array along a path.

name: HATCHEDIT
description: Modifies an existing hatch's pattern, scale, angle, origin and boundaries via the contextual ribbon or dialog. Reach for it when a hatch reads too dense at the plotted scale or needs a new boundary picked up.

name: SPLINEDIT
description: Edits a spline's fit points or control vertices, changes its tolerance, and can convert it to a polyline. Useful for tidying traced contours before they drive offsets or 3D surfaces.

name: LAYER
description: Opens the Layer Properties Manager to create, name, and control the colour, linetype, lineweight, plot and visibility state of every layer. The organisational heart of any drawing built to office or BS/ISO layer standards.

name: LAYISO
description: Isolates the layers of the selected objects by locking and fading, or switching off, every other layer. Ideal for concentrating on the structural grid or one service run in a crowded plan.

name: LAYUNISO
description: Restores the layer states that were in force before the last LAYISO, ending the isolation. Always pair it with LAYISO rather than switching layers back on by hand.

name: LAYFRZ
description: Freezes the layer of each object you pick, hiding it and excluding it from regeneration. Quicker than hunting names in the Layer Manager when you can simply point at the offending linework.

name: LAYTHW
description: Thaws all frozen layers in one go, making them visible and active again. The blanket undo for a session of LAYFRZ picks.

name: LAYOFF
description: Turns off the layer of each object you select, hiding that linework from view. Useful mid-command when background information is getting in the way of picking.

name: LAYON
description: Turns every layer in the drawing back on, restoring anything hidden with LAYOFF. Frozen layers are unaffected and need LAYTHW instead.

name: LAYMCH
description: Moves selected objects onto the layer of another object you point at. A fast way to correct linework drawn on the wrong layer without opening any palettes.

name: LAYCUR
description: Moves selected objects onto the current layer. Handy at the end of a drafting burst when new geometry ended up scattered across whatever layers were current at the time.

name: LAYDEL
description: Deletes a layer together with every object on it, and purges the layer from the drawing. More forceful than PURGE, so use it deliberately when stripping surveys or imported files.

name: LAYMRG
description: Merges the contents of one or more layers onto a target layer and removes the emptied layers. The tidy way to rationalise near-duplicate layers in drawings received from consultants.

name: LAYWALK
description: Steps through layers one or several at a time, showing only their contents while the dialog is open. An excellent audit tool for discovering what actually lives on each layer of an unfamiliar drawing.

name: LAYERSTATE
description: Saves and restores named snapshots of layer visibility, colour and plot settings. Lets one model serve several outputs, such as a general arrangement state and a demolition state, without duplicating the drawing.

name: PROPERTIES
description: Opens the Properties palette showing every editable property of the current selection, from layer and linetype to text height and hatch scale. Leave it docked: it is the fastest way to interrogate and correct objects.

name: LTSCALE
description: Sets the global scale factor applied to all linetypes, controlling how dashed and dotted lines display. Getting LTSCALE (with PSLTSCALE for layouts) right is the difference between readable dashed lines and lines that look continuous.

name: LINETYPE
description: Loads linetype definitions and sets the current linetype for new objects. Architects load dashed, hidden and centre linetypes here for demolition work, items above, and gridlines.

name: LWEIGHT
description: Sets the current lineweight and controls whether lineweights display on screen. Line weight hierarchy — heavy cut lines, light background — is fundamental to drawing legibility, though many offices drive it by layer or plot style instead.

name: COLOR
description: Sets the colour for newly drawn objects, ideally left as ByLayer so colour stays under layer control. Explicit colours are best reserved for exceptions, since many offices map plot pens by colour.

name: BLOCK
description: Defines a named block from selected objects with a chosen base point, stored inside the current drawing. Blocks keep repeated elements — doors, sanitaryware, drawing symbols — consistent, lightweight and countable.

name: INSERT
description: Places a block from the current drawing, recent files or libraries via the Blocks palette, with scale and rotation set on the way in. The everyday route to populating plans with standard components.

name: WBLOCK
description: Writes a block definition or selected objects out to a separate DWG file. The standard way to build an office block library or extract part of a drawing to send to a consultant.

name: BEDIT
description: Opens a block definition in the Block Editor for editing geometry and adding dynamic parameters, actions and constraints. Changes ripple through every insertion when you save, which is exactly why blocks beat loose geometry.

name: XREF
description: Opens the External References palette to attach, reload, unload and repath referenced drawings, images and PDFs. Xrefs underpin coordinated working: the site plan, structural grid and services stay live links rather than stale copies.

name: XATTACH
description: Attaches another DWG as an external reference, with choices of attachment or overlay, insertion point and path type. Overlay is usually the safer choice to avoid circular nesting between team files.

name: ATTACH
description: Attaches an external file — DWG, image, PDF or point cloud — as a referenced underlay in the current drawing. The usual first step when drawing over a scanned survey or a consultant's PDF.

name: XCLIP
description: Crops an xref or block to a rectangular or polygonal boundary so only the relevant portion displays. Perfect for showing just your site from a wider OS map or estate-wide survey.

name: ATTDEF
description: Creates an attribute definition — a named, editable text placeholder — to be included in a block. The mechanism behind intelligent title blocks and tagged symbols whose values can be edited and extracted per insertion.

name: ATTEDIT
description: Edits attribute values in a block insertion, with a legacy option set for global changes across many insertions. For a friendlier single-block dialog, EATTEDIT (or a double-click) is the modern route.

name: EATTEDIT
description: Opens the Enhanced Attribute Editor to change an insertion's attribute values, text styling and layers in one dialog. This is what runs when you double-click a title block to fill in drawing numbers and revisions.

name: REFEDIT
description: Edits a block or xref in place, in the context of the host drawing, saving changes back to the source definition. Convenient for small coordinated tweaks, though editing the xref file directly is often cleaner for big changes.

name: PURGE
description: Removes unused named items — blocks, layers, linetypes, styles and more — plus zero-length geometry and empty text. Regular purging keeps issued files lean and stops obsolete standards propagating between projects.

name: ADCENTER
description: Opens DesignCenter for browsing other drawings and dragging in their blocks, layers, styles and layouts. A quick way to borrow a title block or layer set from a previous project without opening the file.

name: BASE
description: Sets the insertion base point used when the current drawing is inserted or xreffed into another. Setting a sensible base — a grid intersection or site datum — saves everyone downstream from placing your file by eye.

name: COUNT
description: Counts block insertions across the drawing or a selected area and reports them in a palette, with an option to insert the result as a table. Invaluable for checking door, luminaire or parking counts against schedules.

name: DIM
description: The unified dimensioning command: hover over objects and it infers linear, aligned, angular, radial or diameter dimensions, staying active for a run of them. A modern one-stop alternative to picking individual DIM commands.

name: DIMLINEAR
description: Creates a horizontal or vertical dimension between two points or along a picked object. The staple of orthogonal architectural dimensioning, from overall widths down to opening sizes.

name: DIMALIGNED
description: Creates a dimension whose line runs parallel to the two points being measured. The right choice for splayed walls, raking roofs and anything not aligned to the drawing axes.

name: DIMANGULAR
description: Dimensions the angle between two lines, within an arc, or defined by three points. Used for splay angles, roof pitches and setting-out bearings on plans.

name: DIMRADIUS
description: Dimensions the radius of an arc or circle with an R-prefixed value and leader. Standard for curved walls, kerb radii and filleted details.

name: DIMDIAMETER
description: Dimensions the diameter of a circle or arc with the diameter symbol. The convention for pipes, ducts, bolt holes and circular openings.

name: DIMARC
description: Dimensions the length along an arc rather than its chord or radius, marked with an arc symbol. Useful for curved facades and handrails where the developed length is what gets fabricated.

name: DIMORDINATE
description: Creates ordinate dimensions giving X or Y distances from the current UCS origin along a leader. Common for setting-out drawings where every point is referenced to a site datum.

name: DIMCONTINUE
description: Chains a run of dimensions end to end from the last extension line, keeping them on one line. The natural way to dimension a string of rooms or window openings along an elevation.

name: DIMBASELINE
description: Stacks successive dimensions measured from a common first extension line, offset at a set spacing. Suits setting-out from a single datum such as a gridline or party wall.

name: QDIM
description: Generates a whole series of dimensions — continuous, baseline, staggered or ordinate — from one selection of geometry. A time-saver for dimensioning a full elevation of openings in one pass.

name: DIMSTYLE
description: Opens the Dimension Style Manager controlling arrows, text, units, tolerances and fit for every dimension style. Office dimensioning standards live here; set styles up properly once and every drawing benefits.

name: DIMEDIT
description: Modifies existing dimensions: rotating or replacing text, obliquing extension lines, or restoring home positions. The Oblique option is the standard trick for dimensioning isometric views.

name: DIMBREAK
description: Adds a break in a dimension or extension line where it crosses another object or dimension. Keeps dense dimension strings legible where lines would otherwise overlap.

name: DIMSPACE
description: Adjusts the spacing between parallel dimension lines to a set value, or aligns them flush. The quick tidy-up after a stack of baseline dimensions drifts out of rhythm.

name: MLEADER
description: Draws a multileader: an arrowed leader with attached text or a block, governed by a multileader style. The modern standard for keynotes and call-outs, replacing the older QLEADER workflow.

name: MLEADERSTYLE
description: Manages multileader styles: arrowheads, landing lengths, text or block content and annotative scaling. Set once per office standard so every call-out on every sheet matches.

name: QLEADER
description: Draws a leader with attached annotation using its own settings dialog, from the era before multileaders. Still typed out of habit by long-time users, though MLEADER is the maintained tool.

name: TOLERANCE
description: Creates a geometric tolerance feature control frame with symbols, datums and tolerance values. More common in fabrication and engineering drawings than architectural sets, but useful for steelwork and precast interfaces.

name: TABLESTYLE
description: Defines table styles: title, header and data row formatting, borders and text styles. Keeps schedules visually consistent across a drawing set.

name: TEXTSTYLE
description: Manages text styles: font, height behaviour, width factor and annotative scaling for TEXT, MTEXT, dimensions and leaders. Defining a small set of office styles here prevents the font free-for-all that plagues shared drawings.

name: SCALETEXT
description: Rescales multiple text objects about their individual insertion points so they do not drift from their locations. The safe way to change text heights en masse when a drawing moves to a different plot scale.

name: TEXTEDIT
description: Opens any text, mtext or dimension text for in-place editing, the same as double-clicking it. The typed route is quicker when your hands are already on the keyboard.

name: SPELL
description: Runs a spelling check across the drawing or a selection, covering text, mtext, dimensions and attributes. Worth a pass before issuing, since drawing notes rarely get proofread any other way.

name: CENTERMARK
description: Places an associative centre mark at the centre of a circle or arc that updates if the geometry moves or resizes. Standard practice on setting-out and fabrication details for holes and columns.

name: CENTERLINE
description: Creates an associative centreline between two selected lines, staying centred as they move. Useful for duct runs, corridors and symmetrical details where the centreline is a real reference.

name: LAYOUT
description: Creates, copies, renames, deletes and manages paper space layouts. Each layout is one printable sheet, so a plan file typically carries a layout per issued drawing.

name: MVIEW
description: Creates rectangular or polygonal floating viewports on a layout, each showing a view of model space at its own scale. The mechanism by which one model appears at 1:100 on the GA and 1:5 on the details.

name: VPORTS
description: Splits the model space screen into tiled viewports, or creates floating viewports from named configurations on a layout. Working plan-and-3D side by side in model space is a common use.

name: PAGESETUP
description: Defines the printer, paper size, plot area, scale and plot style table for a layout, saved as a named setup. Getting page setups right once per template makes plotting a one-click affair for the whole team.

name: PLOT
description: Prints the current layout or model view to a device or file such as PDF, using a page setup or ad-hoc settings. The final step of almost every drawing task; PREVIEW first saves paper and embarrassment.

name: PREVIEW
description: Shows the drawing exactly as it will plot, including lineweights and plot styles. A quick sanity check for masked text, wrong pen weights and stray viewport frames before committing to an issue.

name: PUBLISH
description: Batch-plots a list of layouts from one or many drawings to a printer, PDF or DWF, optionally as a single multi-sheet file. The tool for issuing a whole drawing package in one operation.

name: EXPORTPDF
description: Exports the current layout or model space directly to a PDF with control over quality, layers and hyperlinks. Quicker than the PLOT dialog when a PDF is all you need.

name: VIEWBASE
description: Generates 2D base drawing views on a layout from a 3D model in the drawing or from Inventor, with projected views to follow. Bridges 3D modelling and conventional orthographic sheets without manual redrawing.

name: MSPACE
description: Switches from paper space into a floating viewport so you can pan, zoom and edit the model through it. Remember to lock the viewport afterwards to protect its scale.

name: PSPACE
description: Returns from a floating viewport to paper space, where title blocks, borders and sheet notes live. The counterpart to MSPACE when working on layouts.

name: OSNAP
description: Configures running object snaps — endpoint, midpoint, centre, intersection and more — and F3 toggles them on and off. Precise drawing in AutoCAD is built on osnaps; drafting without them is guesswork.

name: ORTHO
description: Constrains cursor movement to horizontal and vertical, toggled with F8 even mid-command. The default state for most orthogonal building drafting, released momentarily for the odd splay.

name: SNAP
description: Restricts cursor picks to a set grid increment, toggled with F9. Useful for early block planning on a planning grid; most detailed drafting relies on osnaps and typed distances instead.

name: GRID
description: Displays a reference grid of lines or dots at a set spacing, toggled with F7. A visual aid for judging scale and rhythm rather than a drawing constraint in itself.

name: DSETTINGS
description: Opens the Drafting Settings dialog covering snap and grid, polar tracking (F10), object snaps, object snap tracking (F11) and dynamic input (F12). The one dialog that tunes nearly all the precision aids.

name: DYNMODE
description: Controls dynamic input: the cursor-side dimension fields and prompts that let you type lengths and angles without watching the command line. F12 toggles it; some drafters swear by it, others switch it straight off.

name: UCS
description: Repositions and rotates the user coordinate system, aligning the drawing axes to an object, a face or picked points. Rotating the UCS to a splayed wing lets you draft it orthogonally, then World brings everything back.

name: PLAN
description: Rotates the view to look straight down on the current, a named, or the world UCS. The quick way home after working in a rotated or 3D coordinate system.

name: UCSICON
description: Controls whether the UCS icon is visible, and whether it sits at the origin or the corner of the screen. Worth knowing simply to declutter screenshots or restore the icon when it goes missing.

name: UNITS
description: Sets the drawing's linear and angular unit types, display precision and the insertion scale unit. UK practice is decimal units drawn in millimetres; the insertion unit setting is what stops xrefs arriving 25.4 times too large.

name: LIMITS
description: Defines a rectangular working area for the drawing and can restrict picks to it, also governing the grid display extent. Largely a legacy setting now, but it still appears in drawing setup checklists and templates.

name: DIST
description: Reports the distance, delta X and Y, and angle between two picked points. The everyday measuring tape: checking a corridor width or door clearance takes seconds.

name: MEASUREGEOM
description: Measures distance, radius, angle, area and volume from one command, with a Quick mode that reads dimensions live as you hover. Quick mode has largely replaced separate DIST and AREA calls for on-the-fly checking.

name: AREA
description: Calculates area and perimeter from picked points or a selected object, with add and subtract modes for composite shapes. The direct route to room and site areas; pair with BOUNDARY to measure enclosed spaces cleanly.

name: LIST
description: Prints a full database report on selected objects: type, layer, coordinates, lengths and areas. The forensic tool for interrogating mystery geometry in inherited drawings.

name: ID
description: Reports the X, Y, Z coordinates of a picked point. Useful for checking a setting-out point against schedule values or confirming a drawing sits at the right site coordinates.

name: QUICKCALC
description: Opens a calculator palette that handles arithmetic, unit conversion and coordinate functions, and can feed results straight into a running command. Handy for rise-and-going checks and converting imperial survey figures.

name: FIND
description: Searches for and optionally replaces text across the drawing, including mtext, attributes, dimensions and tables. The fast fix when a room name or drawing number changes throughout a set.

name: QSELECT
description: Builds a selection set by filtering on object type and property values, such as every circle on a given layer. Ideal for bulk corrections like moving all rogue red text to the proper standard.

name: SELECTSIMILAR
description: Extends the selection to every object matching the chosen ones by type and key properties, based on its settings. Pick one door block and instantly hold them all — quicker than QSELECT for like-for-like grabs.

name: GROUP
description: Bundles selected objects into a named or unnamed group that selects as one but stays individually editable. A lighter-weight alternative to blocks for furniture arrangements and repeated assemblies still in flux.

name: UNGROUP
description: Dissolves a group back into its independent member objects. Use it when an arrangement has settled and the grouping is no longer earning its keep.

name: ISOLATEOBJECTS
description: Hides everything except the selected objects, regardless of layer. Sharper than layer isolation when the clutter shares layers with what you need; UNISOLATEOBJECTS brings it all back.

name: HIDEOBJECTS
description: Temporarily hides just the selected objects, the inverse of ISOLATEOBJECTS. Useful for tucking a dimension string or overlapping block out of the way while working underneath it.

name: UNISOLATEOBJECTS
description: Reveals all objects hidden by ISOLATEOBJECTS or HIDEOBJECTS. Run it before saving and issuing, or hidden work can be forgotten entirely.

name: ZOOM
description: Changes view magnification with options for window, extents, previous, object and scale. Zoom Extents (double-click the wheel) is the reflex for finding stray geometry flung miles from the drawing.

name: PAN
description: Slides the view across the drawing without changing magnification, usually done by holding the mouse wheel. The typed command remains useful on laptops and for precise, constrained panning.

name: REGEN
description: Regenerates the drawing display in the current viewport, recomputing curve smoothness and refreshing artefacts; REGENALL does the same across all viewports. The cure when circles display as polygons after deep zooming.

name: VIEW
description: Saves and restores named views of the drawing, including camera position and layer snapshot options. Named views speed up jumping between blocks of a large site plan and can drive sheet viewports.

name: 3DORBIT
description: Rotates the viewpoint freely around a 3D model, also reachable by Shift plus the mouse wheel. The basic navigation for inspecting massing models and checking 3D geometry from all sides.

name: VSCURRENT
description: Sets the current visual style — 2D wireframe, hidden, shaded, conceptual, realistic or X-ray — for the viewport. The quick way to switch a massing model from linework to shaded for a design review; SHADEMODE is the older name for the same job.

name: NAVVCUBE
description: Shows or hides the ViewCube, the corner widget for snapping to top, front, isometric and other standard viewpoints. Clicking Top with north up is often faster than typing view commands.

name: GEOMCONSTRAINT
description: Applies geometric constraints — coincident, parallel, perpendicular, tangent, equal and others — that hold relationships as geometry is edited. The foundation of parametric 2D sketching for adaptable detail and product drawings.

name: DIMCONSTRAINT
description: Adds dimensional constraints that drive geometry: change the value and the linework updates to match. Combined with geometric constraints it turns a standard detail into a small parametric model.

name: DELCONSTRAINT
description: Removes all geometric and dimensional constraints from the selected objects. The clean exit when constrained geometry needs to become ordinary linework again.

name: EXTRUDE
description: Pushes a closed profile or region into a 3D solid, or an open curve into a surface, along a height, path or taper (ribbon location applies in the 3D Modelling workspace). The quickest step from a floor plan outline to a massing block.

name: REVOLVE
description: Spins a profile around an axis to form a solid or surface of revolution. The natural tool for domes, columns, balusters and turned details.

name: SWEEP
description: Drives a profile along a path curve to create a solid or surface, with twist and scale options. Ideal for handrails, mouldings, kerbs and services runs following a route.

name: LOFT
description: Builds a solid or surface through a series of cross-section profiles, optionally guided by rails or a path. Suits transitions between different sections, such as a duct reducer or a sculpted canopy.

name: PRESSPULL
description: Extrudes or cuts by clicking inside any bounded area or on a face and dragging, inferring the boundary automatically. The most intuitive way to raise walls from a plan or punch openings through a solid.

name: POLYSOLID
description: Draws wall-like solids of set width and height directly, like a 3D polyline, or converts existing lines and polylines into them. A fast route to modelled walls from a sketch plan.

name: BOX
description: Creates a solid rectangular box from a base rectangle and height, or as a cube. The primitive behind quick massing studies and boolean cutting blocks.

name: CYLINDER
description: Creates a solid cylinder from a circular or elliptical base and height. Used for columns, tanks and as a cutting tool for circular openings.

name: UNION
description: Fuses two or more solids, surfaces or regions into a single object. The first of the three booleans used to consolidate a massing model from primitives.

name: SUBTRACT
description: Removes one set of solids or regions from another, leaving the difference. The standard way to cut window and door openings out of modelled walls.

name: INTERSECT
description: Keeps only the overlapping volume of the selected solids or regions, discarding the rest. Useful for finding clashes or carving a form to a site envelope.

name: SLICE
description: Cuts solids or surfaces along a plane or surface, keeping one or both halves. The direct way to take a section through a massing model or trim a solid to a level.

name: THICKEN
description: Gives a surface a uniform thickness, converting it into a solid. Turns a lofted or swept roof surface into a build-up you can section and measure.

name: 3DMOVE
description: Moves objects in 3D using a gizmo that constrains motion to an axis or plane. Safer than plain MOVE in 3D work, where an unintended shift in Z is easy to miss.

name: 3DROTATE
description: Rotates objects about the X, Y or Z axis using a ribbon-style gizmo picked on screen. The controlled way to stand a drawn elevation up vertically or tilt a roof plane.

name: 3DALIGN
description: Aligns objects in 3D by matching up to three source points to three destination points, moving and rotating in one step. Ideal for seating an imported component onto a face at the correct orientation.

name: NEW
description: Starts a new drawing from a chosen template (DWT). Always start from the office template so layers, styles and page setups arrive ready-made.

name: OPEN
description: Opens an existing drawing, with options for read-only and partial open of selected layouts or layers. Partial open is worth remembering for enormous survey files.

name: QSAVE
description: Saves the current drawing under its existing name without prompting. Make it a habit; pair with automatic save settings under OPTIONS for belt and braces.

name: SAVEAS
description: Saves the drawing under a new name, location or DWG version. Saving back to an older DWG format is routine when consultants run earlier releases.

name: CLOSE
description: Closes the current drawing, prompting to save unsaved changes; CLOSEALL shuts every open drawing. Keeping the open-file count down helps performance and concentration alike.

name: AUDIT
description: Checks the open drawing's database for errors and optionally fixes them, reporting what it found. Run it on any file that behaves oddly, and routinely on drawings received from outside.

name: RECOVER
description: Opens a damaged drawing while repairing it, more thorough than AUDIT on an already-open file. The first resort when a DWG refuses to open normally.

name: ETRANSMIT
description: Packages the drawing with all its xrefs, fonts, plot styles and images into a transmittal set, typically a zip. The professional way to issue CAD files so nothing arrives broken or missing at the other end.

name: DWGCOMPARE
description: Compares the current drawing with another and colour-codes the differences, with revision clouds available for changed areas. Invaluable for spotting what a consultant altered between issues.

name: OPTIONS
description: Opens the application settings dialog: file paths, display colours, save intervals, plotting defaults, selection behaviour and more. Where you set automatic save, crosshair size and the template search path.

name: CUI
description: Opens the Customise User Interface editor for ribbons, toolbars, keyboard shortcuts and command aliases. The power-user route to shaping AutoCAD around an office's workflow.

name: COMMANDLINE
description: Restores the command line window when it has been closed, with Ctrl+9 toggling it. Top of every list of panic fixes, because AutoCAD without a command line is barely AutoCAD.

name: UNDO
description: Reverses previous operations, with the full UNDO command offering marks, groups and multi-step control; the U alias steps back once. The safety net that makes bold drafting possible.

name: REDO
description: Reinstates operations reversed by UNDO, with MREDO handling several at once. Only valid immediately after an undo, so it pays to decide quickly.

name: RENAME
description: Renames named objects such as blocks, layers, styles and views. The safe way to bring inherited content into your naming convention without recreating it.

name: SHEETSET
description: Opens the Sheet Set Manager, which organises layouts from many drawings into a numbered, publishable set with shared fields. Powerful for large projects where sheet indexes and title block data must stay synchronised.

name: TOOLPALETTES
description: Opens the Tool Palettes window of drag-and-drop blocks, hatches and commands, organised in tabs. A well-curated office palette puts standard details and symbols one drag away.

name: COPYCLIP
description: Copies selected objects to the Windows clipboard for pasting into another drawing or application. For drawing-to-drawing work, COPYBASE with a snapped base point is the more precise cousin.

name: COPYBASE
description: Copies objects to the clipboard together with a picked base point. Essential for pasting geometry into another drawing at an exact snapped location rather than roughly by eye.

name: PASTECLIP
description: Pastes clipboard contents into the drawing, placing AutoCAD objects at a picked point. Objects copied with COPYBASE land by their base point for precise positioning.

name: PASTEBLOCK
description: Pastes clipboard objects as a single anonymous block rather than loose geometry. Keeps pasted content contained and easy to move or delete as one, at the cost of an auto-generated block name.

name: HELP
description: Opens AutoCAD's help system, jumping straight to the reference page for the command currently in progress. Worth pressing mid-command instead of abandoning it to search the web.
